pupils 多指中小学生；undergraduates 指本科生。
raise 常与 standards / awareness 搭配。
discipline 更正式，常指学科领域。

sentences.pattern: One of the main reasons why + subject + verb is that + complete clause.
sentences.example: One of the main reasons why early education matters is that it shapes children’s attitudes towards learning.

sentences.pattern: Subject + can play a crucial role in + noun or gerund.
sentences.cn: 某人或某事能在……中发挥关键作用。
sentences.example: Teachers can play a crucial role in building students’ confidence.

sentences.pattern: While + complete clause, it is equally important to + verb.
sentences.example: While academic knowledge is valuable, it is equally important to develop practical skills.

expressions.text: I’ve always been keen on + noun or gerund.
expressions.example: I’ve always been keen on subjects that involve problem-solving.

expressions.text: It took me a while to + verb.
expressions.example: It took me a while to get used to studying independently.

expressions.text: What I find most useful is + noun phrase.
expressions.example: What I find most useful is the detailed feedback from my tutor.

expressions.text: play a vital role in + noun or gerund
expressions.cn: 在……中发挥至关重要的作用
expressions.example: Parental support can play a vital role in a child’s early education.

expressions.text: have a positive impact on + noun
expressions.example: Constructive feedback can have a positive impact on academic performance.

mistakes.why: knowledge 通常与 gain 或 acquire 搭配，不能说 learn knowledge。
discuss 本身已经表示“讨论”，后面不能再加 about。

mistakes.wrong: Education can bring many benefits for students.
mistakes.correct: Education can bring many benefits to students.
mistakes.why: 表示“给某人带来好处”时，使用 bring benefits to somebody。

writingIdeas.topicSentence: Accessible education can enable people from disadvantaged backgrounds to improve their long-term prospects.
writingIdeas.argument: High-quality education gives learners the knowledge and qualifications required for stable employment. This matters particularly to students from low-income families, who may have fewer professional contacts or financial resources. By improving their career prospects, education can increase their earnings and reduce the disadvantages passed from one generation to the next. For example, an affordable vocational course may lead directly to skilled work that was previously inaccessible. Education can therefore promote social mobility when access is genuinely equitable.

writingIdeas.viewpoint: Schools should teach practical life skills.
writingIdeas.topicSentence: A balanced curriculum should prepare students for everyday responsibilities as well as examinations.
writingIdeas.argument: Academic subjects provide essential knowledge, but they do not cover every responsibility that school-leavers will face. Many young adults struggle to budget, communicate professionally or evaluate financial information because these skills have never been taught explicitly. Short, practical lessons could allow students to apply such knowledge before they enter the workforce. For instance, learners might compare rental contracts or prepare a realistic monthly budget. A balanced curriculum would consequently prepare students for examinations and independent adult life.

speaking.question: What subject did you enjoy most at school?
speaking.answer: I probably enjoyed history the most. I liked the way one event could be explained from several points of view, so the lessons felt more like solving a puzzle than memorising dates. I also had a teacher who told great stories, which made a huge difference.

speaking.question: Do you prefer studying alone or with other people?
speaking.answer: Most of the time, I prefer studying alone because I can work at my own pace and focus on what I find difficult. That said, a small study group is useful before an exam. Explaining an idea to someone else quickly shows me whether I really understand it.

reading.title: Beyond the Examination Hall
paragraphs: A. For much of the twentieth century, formal education was organised primarily around the transfer of information. Teachers presented established knowledge, students recorded it, and examinations measured how accurately it could be recalled. This model was efficient when books were scarce and access to reliable information was limited. Since the 1990s, however, digital technology has made facts available almost instantly, prompting educators to reconsider what schools should enable learners to do with knowledge rather than merely how much they can remember.

B. Research on classroom learning has consequently placed greater emphasis on critical thinking. In a review of studies from several education systems, researchers found that students understood complex ideas more securely when they had to compare evidence, explain a conclusion and apply a concept to an unfamiliar problem. This does not mean that factual knowledge has become unnecessary. By contrast, a learner cannot evaluate an argument about climate or economics without first understanding the relevant principles and terminology.

C. Project-based learning is one attempt to combine knowledge with its practical application. Students might investigate a local transport problem, analyse survey data and present a proposal, drawing on mathematics, geography and communication skills. Nevertheless, critics note that such work is difficult to assess consistently. A standardised examination produces results that can be compared across thousands of candidates, whereas a group project may conceal substantial differences in individual effort. Some schools have therefore introduced mixed assessment rather than abandoning examinations altogether.

D. The debate ultimately concerns preparation for an uncertain labour market. Technical knowledge may become outdated, while the ability to learn independently retains value across different occupations. Yet treating knowledge and transferable skills as competing goals creates a false choice. A well-rounded curriculum requires carefully selected content, repeated opportunities to apply it and assessment that measures both secure understanding and effective use. The central challenge is not to replace traditional learning, but to develop a more productive relationship between knowledge and action.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct heading for Paragraph C.
options: The continuing value of factual knowledge
A practical approach and its assessment problem
Technology as a substitute for teachers
questions.explanation: Paragraph C describes project-based learning and then explains why it is difficult to assess consistently.

questions.prompt: The reviewed studies found that students learned complex ideas better when they explained and applied them.
questions.explanation: Paragraph B reports stronger understanding when students compared evidence, explained conclusions and applied concepts.

questions.prompt: Group projects may hide differences in each student’s ______.
questions.explanation: Paragraph C states that a group project may conceal differences in individual effort.
